context:
Goal: the Ask area holds only what still needs your eyes.
Problem (goal): asks pile up and you rarely read the area, so it needs a rule for when an ask leaves, and how it leaves is your call.
Based on (read): your comment on the Ask area (Nov 10, 09:11 CST) says it is too crowded, and that an ask must become a page question or a roadmap step with a short reply, never just vanish.
Departs from: main — adds a phase-out rule for asks.
Meanwhile: asks route as today, and step ask-phase-out waits for your answer.

options.gain: A short area, and nothing is lost.
options.how: Once routed, an ask folds to one line naming its home (step:<slug> or item N), and leaves after you open it.
options.label: Fold to its home once routed (Recommended)
options.lose: The full text is one click away.

options.how: An ask over 24 h old moves to an archive tab.
options.label: Archive asks older than 24 h
options.lose: An ask nobody routed can hide in the archive.

options.how: An ask leaves only when you close it.
options.label: You close each ask

ref: owner comment, Ask area thread b2ff97bf, Nov 10 09:11 CST
reply:
Routed 09:16 CST Nov 10: pick a with your read-receipt note. A routed ask or answered item shows one line (its home and the short reply); you press Mark read and it leaves; nothing is deleted. It covers the Ask area and the Answered row. Home: step ask-phase-out.
Where this question was (your 10:51 CST comment on the Answered row): triage posted it as item 480 at 09:13 CST Nov 10, for the coordinator, from your 09:11 CST comment on the Ask area. You answered it at 09:14 CST (a, with the read-receipt note), so it closed and left the page before the Mark read button exists. The button is step ask-phase-out, held by the freeze.
title: How should an ask leave the Ask area?
why: Recommended: a. The area stays short and every ask keeps a home you can open.
